result:
No actions yet. One choice needs to be theirs before I write.

---

Understood, I'll write it up. One decision is still open, and it changes the whole design, so I'd rather you make it than have me assume it. It's where the batch tracking lives:

1. **Inside the existing taproom app** (my recommendation). Add batches, sacks and bottling runs as new tables in the same SQLite database, with new pages in the same Flask app on the Pi. There's one thing to run, back up and log into, and it reuses what's already working. The cost is that brewing records and taproom tabs share one database, so a bad change to one could affect the other. Careful structure inside the app keeps that contained.
2. **A separate small app on the same Pi**, with its own database. Your trace records stay fully apart from the tabs, which matters if those records ever have to stand up in a recall. The cost is two apps to start, update and back up.

I left out off-the-shelf brewery software because you asked for something built into what you have.

I recommend option 1. It's the least for you to look after, and the tracking is small enough to sit cleanly beside the tabs.

Once you pick, I'll write the design. A reviewer will read it before I hand it to you. If that reviewer finds something only you can answer, I'll come back once with a short list. The project folder isn't under version control yet, so I'll also set that up to save the design.

Which one should I go with?
